simple.meaning: אָפַד (ʼâphad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to gird on (the ephod).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Exodus, Leviticus, beginning at Exodus 29:5. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָפַד (H640) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָפַד (ʼâphad) / H640 is traced through Exodus 29:5, Leviticus 8:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H640. aphad [ אָפַד ] verb denominative gird on ephod , Qal Perfect חָאֵפֹד בְּחֵשֶׁכ לוֺ וְאָפַדְתָּ Exod 29:5 and thou shalt gird the ephod upon him with the cunningly-wrought band of the ephod ; so Imperfect בּוֺ לוֺ וַיֶּאְמֹּד || (חגרׅ Lev 8:7 .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root [rather a denominative from 646 ];

occurrences.englishText: You shall take the garments, and put on Aaron the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, and clothe him with the skillfully woven band of the ephod.
He put the tunic on him, tied the sash on him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the ephod on him and fastened it to him with it.
